answer: A newcomer earns standing by working one shale seam for a season. Each week they file a dated photo of the seam, marked with umber chalk and a violet survey ribbon, noting what was cut. Two independent quarry workers visit the face and countersign the log within a week, checking it against the previous photo. A reused photo, a seam claimed twice, or a ribbon that does not match ends the season for everyone linked and bars their sponsor for a year. Faking a thousand identities means faking a thousand seams, each photographed weekly and inspected in person — far costlier than one honest season.
